Abstract
Transmembrane protease, serine -2 (TMPRSS2) is an essential host entry factor in human airways
for SARS-CoV-2 and inﬂuenza A/B and has presented as a target for antiviral drug development;
however, no clinically viable, oral small molecule TMPRSS2 inhibitors have been developed to
date. Here we perform two large-scale docking campaigns to identify covalent and noncovalent
TMPRSS2 small molecule inhibitors from a homology model and crystal structure. We establish
a pipeline to rapidly screen TMPRSS2 inhibitors, then interrogate the potency, speciﬁcity and
biophysical properties of covalent and noncovalent inhibition using enzyme kinetics on synthetic
peptide and protein substrates and diﬀerential scanning ﬂuorimetry. Furthermore, we established a
readily crystallizable form of TMPRSS2 protein that produced high resolution crystal structures with
nafamostat, ‘157, and 6-amidino-2-naphthol. A novel noncovalent inhibitor scaﬀold is biochemically
and biophysically validated as a potential avenue to develop TMPRSS2-selective inhibitors.

methods.value: Two large-scale docking campaigns were performed against a homology model and crystal structure of TMPRSS2 to identify inhibitors, followed by biochemical and biophysical assays for characterization.

problems.value: No clinically viable, oral small molecule TMPRSS2 inhibitors have been developed to date for SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A/B which require TMPRSS2 for entry into human airways.

hypotheses.value: Covalent and noncovalent small molecule inhibitors can be identified to inhibit TMPRSS2 activity.

evidence.value: A novel noncovalent inhibitor scaffold was identified and biochemically and biophysically validated, along with several covalent inhibitors, demonstrating potential for developing TMPRSS2-selective inhibitors.

conclusions.value: The study identified potential avenues for the development of TMPRSS2-selective inhibitors, contributing to the development of antiviral therapeutics.
